Use case: precise-object-edit / actual 2D animation source drawings.
Asset: eight production body attachments for Mongdol's FORWARD SOMERSAULT toward the viewer. These actual drawings will be sliced and used in the game animation; this is NOT a presentation or preview.
Reference image 1 is the complete approved footless stone body and the exact appearance authority. Reference image 2 is the approved original character for sandstone material and proportions only. Keep the same wide squat golden-ochre faceted rock, same volume, two small dark teal eyes, deep teal outline, subtle painterly texture and upper-left illumination.
Output one genuine transparent PNG, exactly FOUR columns by TWO rows of equal square cells, ideally 2048x1024. One COMPLETE footless stone body per cell. Cell order left to right, top to bottom. In each cell horizontal center at 50%, contact baseline at 86%, the same body width about 62% of cell width, consistent volume and ample transparent margin. Camera is fixed slightly elevated front view. The body stays broad left-to-right at every pitch angle. Reconstruct real newly exposed top, underside and back surfaces, with changed perspective and coherent facet occlusion.
Motion axis is HORIZONTAL LEFT-TO-RIGHT THROUGH THE BODY: the top moves forward toward the viewer and down. This is an end-over-end front tumble, like a forward somersault on a floor. NOT a clockwise cartwheel in the picture plane, NOT a coin rotating flat, NOT sideways rolling. Never rotate the face sideways; the two eyes remain a left-right pair when visible.
The eight actual phase attachments:
cell 0: pitch 0 degrees, approved frontal reference pose, eyes in original front face.
cell 1: pitch forward 45 degrees, front face tilts DOWN, eyes approach the lower front edge and are partly foreshortened, much more upper surface exposed.
cell 2: pitch forward 90 degrees, former top surface faces the viewer, front/eyes face down and are hidden; no eyes. Solid broad rounded-faceted ochre stone.
cell 3: pitch forward 135 degrees, former top continues downward, rear surface comes around from above; no eyes.
cell 4: pitch forward 180 degrees, backside faces viewer, original underside is uppermost; no eyes, a believable completed back and underside, still the same one stone.
cell 5: pitch forward 225 degrees, underside rolls toward viewer while back goes down; no eyes.
cell 6: pitch forward 270 degrees, original front face points upward; the two eyes begin to reappear together near the upper edge on the upward-facing plane.
cell 7: pitch forward 315 degrees, front face rolls back toward the viewer, eyes visible high on the foreshortened upward-tilted face, ready to return to cell 0.
Keep x width and solid stone volume stable, no rubber squash, no thin flattened disc at quarter turns. No feet in any cell, no arms, mouth, eyebrows, egg, cracks, magic, new accessories, floor or shadow. No grid lines, dividers, captions, numbers or labels. Actual alpha transparency, complete unclipped silhouettes, fixed cell registration.
inbetweens:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Production IN-BETWEEN drawings for a 2D forward-somersault body attachment cycle. Actual source artwork, not a preview board.
Reference image 1 is the EXACT approved original footless Mongdol body. Reference image 2 is the eight checked forward-tumble key views: 0,45,90,135 degrees on the top row and 180,225,270,315 on the bottom row. Preserve these checked designs, volume, broad left-right width, faceted stone surfaces, eye placement logic, warm ochre palette, soft brush texture, clean dark teal outline, fixed camera and fixed upper-left illumination.
Draw ONLY the eight missing halfway views between those checked keys. Output a transparent PNG with exactly FOUR columns and TWO rows of equal square cells, same format as reference 2, ideally 1792x896. One full footless stone per cell. Same actual body size as reference 2, about 85% of each cell width, horizontally centered with ample uncut transparent margin. Contact baseline identical across cells. No labels, grid, text or external shadows.
Read left to right then next row:
cell0 pitch 22.5 degrees forward: halfway between key0 and key45. Front tips down, eyes lower slightly, upper surface starts rolling toward viewer.
cell1 pitch 67.5: halfway key45 to key90. Eyes vanish over the bottom edge as original front points into the ground; top face comes fully into view.
cell2 pitch112.5: halfway key90 to key135. No eyes. Former top rolls downward, back surface advances from above.
cell3 pitch157.5: halfway key135 to key180. No eyes. Back nearly faces viewer, underside approaches upper silhouette.
cell4 pitch202.5: halfway key180 to key225. No eyes. Back turns down, underside turns toward viewer.
cell5 pitch247.5: halfway key225 to key270. Underside mostly faces viewer, original face begins to wrap around the upper edge; only the tiny upper tips of the eye pair can start appearing.
cell6 pitch292.5: halfway key270 to key315. Both eyes visible together on the upward-facing upper-front plane, moving downward toward their normal positions.
cell7 pitch337.5: halfway key315 and the ORIGINAL reference 1 neutral pose, almost upright, eyes close to normal front position, original silhouette and material nearly restored.
Every phase rotates end-over-end about a HORIZONTAL LEFT-TO-RIGHT BODY AXIS toward viewer. No sideways tilt of the eye pair, no screen-plane cartwheel, no thin coin shape, no stretch/squash. New back/top/underside surfaces are drawn with physically consistent overlap and preserve stone volume. Same fixed view and broad width in all cells. Genuine alpha background. No feet, limbs, mouths, eyebrows, eggs, cracks, magic, floor, scenery or extra objects.
